description: Negative corpus for AC-112: ordinary Chinese and English sentences that contain no identifier at all. Every sentence must come back byte-identical from repairIdentifiers(). The dangerous entries are the ones carrying a `near` span — an ordinary phrase one edit distance away from a real file name in this repository — because a matcher that thresholds on similarity alone rewrites exactly those. Unrelated sentences cannot fail this test; near-misses can.
nearSemantics: `near.word` squashed by the module's own normaliser must be at edit distance exactly 1 from `near.of`, and `near.of` must still be a live candidate from `git ls-files`. The runner recomputes both, so the claim cannot rot silently into a comment.
